prompt: In 1 Samuel, what series of events leads to Samuel serving at the tabernacle in Shiloh?
options: Hannah prays for a son, the LORD answers her, and she brings young Samuel to Eli after he is weaned
Samuel is captured from a Philistine village and given to Eli as a servant boy
Eli's sons choose Samuel from among the priests' own sons to replace their father someday when he grows old
Samuel runs away from his family as a child and Eli takes him in as an orphan
explanation: Hannah's vow and prayer are answered with Samuel's birth, and she keeps her promise by giving him to the LORD's service at Shiloh.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what happens to the ark of the covenant after the Philistines capture it in battle?
options: It is kept as a war trophy in the temple of Dagon at Ashdod for years, until Saul's army finally marches on the city and reclaims it by force
The Philistines destroy it right away because they are afraid of its power
It causes disaster wherever it goes among the Philistines until they send it back with a guilt offering
The Philistines successfully add it to their temple worship of Dagon with no trouble at all
explanation: The ark brings plagues on every Philistine city that holds it, until the Philistines send it back to Israel with gifts of gold.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what happens after the elders of Israel demand a king from Samuel?
options: Samuel refuses outright and Israel goes without a king for another generation
The LORD tells Samuel to warn the people what a king will cost them, and Saul is anointed as that king
Samuel appoints his own two sons as co-kings to rule jointly over Israel
The Philistines choose a king for Israel and impose him on the people by force
explanation: Samuel warns Israel what a king will take from them, but the people insist, and Saul is anointed and chosen by lot as their first king.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what two mistakes cost Saul the LORD's favor?
options: He offered a sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel, and he spared King Agag and the best plunder instead of destroying everything
He refused to fight the Philistines at all, and he later fled the battlefield in fear of Goliath
He married a foreign wife, and he built an altar to a foreign god at Gilgal
He disbanded his own army without permission, and he refused to pay his soldiers their wages
explanation: Saul's impatient sacrifice at Gilgal and his failure to fully destroy the Amalekites both lead Samuel to tell him the kingdom will not continue.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, how does David's standing in Saul's house change between his anointing and his flight into the wilderness?
options: He is brought to court as Saul's cupbearer and stays at Saul's side as his most trusted commander until Saul's death
He is anointed in secret, kills Goliath, becomes Jonathan's close friend, and ends up fleeing for his life from a jealous Saul
He is rejected by Saul from the very beginning and never once enters his court
He marries Michal right away and is named Saul's official successor by a public vote
explanation: David rises from shepherd to giant-killer to court favorite, but Saul's growing jealousy eventually forces him to run for his life.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, on what two occasions does David have a chance to kill Saul during his years as a fugitive, and what does he do instead?
options: He finds Saul asleep in a cave and again in his camp, and both times he only takes a small proof of the chance rather than kill him
He captures Saul in open battle twice and both times sets him free unharmed the next morning
He is offered a bounty to kill Saul by the Philistines on two occasions and refuses the bounty both times
He corners Saul at Nob and again at Keilah but is stopped both times by Jonathan's sudden intervention
explanation: David cuts off a piece of Saul's robe in a cave at En Gedi, and later takes his spear and water jug from his camp, refusing to harm the LORD's anointed either time.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what happens to Saul in the days leading up to his death?
options: He wins one final decisive battle against the Philistines before dying peacefully of old age
He is crowned a second time by Samuel's spirit before leading Israel to a great victory
He consults a medium because the LORD will not answer him, hears from Samuel's spirit that he and his sons will die, and is fatally wounded before taking his own life
He abdicates the throne to David in a public ceremony and retires quietly to Gibeah
explanation: Saul seeks out the medium of En-dor, hears Samuel's spirit pronounce his death, and falls on his own sword at Mount Gilboa.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, how does Samuel first respond when he hears his name called at night?
options: He assumes it is Eli calling him and runs to Eli's room
He immediately recognizes the voice as the LORD's and answers right away
He wakes his mother Hannah, who is staying nearby, and asks her what to do
He ignores the voice completely, thinking he only imagined it
explanation: Samuel doesn't yet know the LORD's voice, so he runs to Eli three times before Eli realizes what is happening and tells him how to answer.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Samuel tell Saul about obedience after Saul spares Agag and the best of the plunder?
options: That obeying the LORD's voice matters more than offering sacrifices
That sacrifices always outweigh obedience whenever a king is at war
That Saul should have consulted the priests before deciding either way
That the LORD does not care how a king treats a defeated enemy
explanation: Samuel tells Saul that to obey is better than sacrifice, and that his partial obedience has cost him the kingdom.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, where is Saul found hiding when Samuel is about to present him to Israel as king?
explanation: The LORD reveals that Saul has hidden himself among the baggage, and the people run to bring him out.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, why does Saul become afraid of David after David's early victories?
options: Because the people sing that David has killed even more enemies than Saul has
Because David refuses to fight in any more of Saul's battles
Because Jonathan publicly declares David the rightful king in front of the army
Because the Philistines threaten to attack unless Saul removes David from his court
explanation: When the women sing that Saul has killed thousands but David tens of thousands, Saul grows jealous and afraid of him.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, which two animals does David tell Saul he has killed while guarding his father's sheep, before facing Goliath?
explanation: David has struck down both a lion and a bear that took a lamb from the flock, and says the LORD who delivered him from them will deliver him from Goliath.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what piece of Saul's clothing does David cut a corner from in the cave at En Gedi instead of killing him?
explanation: David secretly cuts off a corner of Saul's robe, and even that troubles his conscience.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does David do after learning that Ziklag has been burned and his family taken captive?
options: He gives up on the pursuit, believing there is nothing left he can do
He strengthens himself in the LORD, inquires whether to pursue, and then chases down and defeats the raiders
He sends a messenger to Saul's army asking for their help in the pursuit
He negotiates a ransom payment with the Amalekites instead of fighting them
explanation: David inquires of the LORD through the ephod, is told to pursue, and recovers everyone and everything the raiders had taken.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Jonathan do at the Philistine garrison before the rest of Saul's army gets involved?
options: He and his armor-bearer climb up and attack the garrison alone, trusting the LORD to give them victory
He sends a spy ahead to count the number of Philistine soldiers stationed there
He negotiates a secret truce with the Philistine commander before any fighting starts
He waits quietly for his father's direct orders before making any move at all
explanation: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb up to the garrison on their own, believing nothing can hinder the LORD from saving by few or many.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Jonathan shoot as a prearranged signal to warn David that Saul intends to kill him?
explanation: Jonathan shoots arrows beyond the boy and calls out the agreed signal, telling David to flee.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what happens to Eli when he hears that the ark of God has been captured?
explanation: At the news of the ark, Eli falls backward from his seat, breaks his neck, and dies.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Abigail do when she learns that Nabal has insulted David's messengers?
options: She hides inside her house and waits to see what David will decide to do
She quickly gathers food and gifts and goes out to meet David before he can take revenge
She sends her own servants out to fight David's men on Nabal's behalf
She sends word to Saul at Gibeah that David is nearby with four hundred armed men, hoping the king's forces will arrive before David does
explanation: Abigail acts quickly on her own, bringing food and a wise appeal to David before he can carry out his plan against Nabal's household.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, how does Michal help David escape when Saul sends men to kill him?
options: She disguises David as one of her own servants and walks him past the guards
She lowers him through a window and puts a household idol in the bed to fool the men sent to watch him
She hides him in a storage room and tells the men he already left the city
She convinces her father in person to call off the men sent after David
explanation: Michal lets David down through a window at night and disguises the household idol as David sleeping to buy him time to escape.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, according to Samuel's warning, what will a king take from the people of Israel once he rules over them?
options: Their sons for his army and chariots, their daughters for his household, and a tenth of their grain, flocks, and produce
Only a small yearly payment in silver from every family in the land
Nothing at all, since Samuel only warns them about foreign kings, not their own
Their firstborn sons as hostages, held at the king's court until each family pays a ransom in silver
explanation: Samuel lists everything a king will take, from sons and daughters to a tenth of their flocks and fields, but the people insist anyway.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what happens to the statue of Dagon after the Philistines place the captured ark in his temple?
options: It remains standing beside the ark for seven months with no incident, until the Philistine lords finally decide to send the ark away
It is found fallen on its face before the ark, and the second time its head and hands are broken off
The Philistine priests quietly move it to a different city to keep it safe
It begins speaking prophecies to the Philistines about the coming war with Israel
explanation: Dagon's statue is found fallen before the ark twice, and the second time it is broken apart, showing whose power is greater.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does the LORD tell Samuel he looks at, when Samuel is impressed by Jesse's oldest son?
explanation: Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does David do that calms Saul whenever the tormenting spirit troubles him?
explanation: David takes the lyre and plays, and the harmful spirit departs from Saul.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does David call Saul when he explains why he will not raise his hand against him?
explanation: David refuses to put out his hand against the LORD's anointed, in the cave and again in Saul's camp.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, how does Saul summon Israel's army to rescue Jabesh-gilead?
options: He sends royal messengers carrying a written proclamation to every town in Israel
He cuts a pair of oxen into pieces and sends them throughout Israel with a warning about what will happen to anyone who doesn't join him
He blows a trumpet from the top of a mountain that can be heard for miles
He asks Samuel to announce the call to arms at the next public assembly
explanation: Saul cuts up a yoke of oxen and sends the pieces through Israel as a vivid warning to anyone who refuses to answer the call.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does David do to escape King Achish's court at Gath?
options: He fights his way out using a hidden weapon he had smuggled in
He pretends to be insane, scratching on the gate and letting saliva run down his beard
He bribes the palace guards with gold to let him slip away quietly
He convinces Achish that Saul has already forgiven him and welcomes him back home to Israel
explanation: Recognized as the man celebrated for killing tens of thousands, David acts insane so Achish's men will let him go rather than harm him.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what warning does the man of God give Eli about his sons Hophni and Phinehas?
options: That they will both die on the same day
That they will be exiled from Israel for the rest of their lives
That they will lose their priestly titles but be allowed to keep their lives
That only one of them will die, while the other repents and is spared
explanation: The man of God tells Eli that both his sons will die on the same day as a sign that the judgment is real.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what rule does David establish about sharing plunder after rescuing the captives from the Amalekites?
options: Only the men who actually fought in the battle get to keep any of the plunder
The plunder is divided strictly by military rank, with commanders receiving a much larger share
Those who stayed behind to guard the supplies share the plunder equally with those who fought
The plunder is given entirely to the families of the captives who were rescued
explanation: David rules that the share of the one who stayed with the supplies must equal the share of the one who went into battle, and this becomes a lasting practice.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Jonathan give David as a sign of the covenant they make with each other?
options: His own robe, armor, sword, and bow
A parcel of land near his father's palace at Gibeah
One of his father's prized war horses
A written copy of the covenant sealed by Samuel himself
explanation: Jonathan strips off his own robe, armor, sword, and bow and gives them to David as part of their covenant.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Jonathan ask David to promise regarding his family when he renews their covenant?
options: That David will never take the throne of Israel for himself
That David will never cut off his steadfast love from Jonathan's house, even when the LORD has cut off David's enemies
That David will marry one of Jonathan's daughters someday
That David will let Jonathan rule as co-king once he becomes king
explanation: Jonathan asks David to show unfailing kindness to his family in the future, and David swears to it as part of their covenant.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does Jonathan tell David when he visits him in the wilderness of Ziph to renew their covenant?
options: That David will surely be king and Jonathan himself will be next to him
That Saul has finally agreed to make peace with David for good
That Jonathan plans to leave Israel and join David permanently in the wilderness
That the Philistines have offered to make David their king instead of Saul
explanation: Jonathan strengthens David's hand in God, telling him he will surely be king and that Jonathan will be second to him.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what do David and Jonathan do when they part after the arrow signal, once they know Saul intends to kill David?
options: They fight one last battle together before finally going their separate ways
They weep together and part after renewing their covenant one more time
They travel together to Ramah to warn Samuel of Saul's plans
They agree never to speak to each other again to protect Jonathan from Saul's suspicion
explanation: David and Jonathan weep together and renew their covenant before David leaves to live as a fugitive.

prompt: In 1 Samuel, what does the text say about how often the LORD was speaking to Israel right before he calls out to young Samuel?
options: The word of the LORD was rare, and visions from him were infrequent
Prophets filled the land, and visions from the LORD came to Israel every day
The LORD had stopped speaking to Israel entirely since the days of Moses
Every household in Israel had its own priest who heard from the LORD directly
explanation: 1 Samuel 3 opens by noting how rare the word of the LORD and visions from him had become, which makes his call to Samuel that night stand out.
